close_reason: Both LintRunner::run_chain and DeviationRunner::run_chain now panic via assert_eq! when kinds.len() != chain.len(); message names both lengths and cites PKIX-7f92.9 for rationale. The default-to-IntermediateCa silent-misclassification path is gone. Two #[should_panic] regression tests lock the behavior (kinds shorter than chain, kinds longer than chain). DeviationRunner::run_chain inherits the same panic shape. No external callers; in-source callers already pass matching-length slices. 290 pkix-lint tests pass; workspace builds clean.
description:
lib.rs:1577-1582 (run_chain) and equivalent in DeviationRunner::run_chain: when kinds.get(i) returns None, the runner defaults to SubjectKind::IntermediateCa. This is documented but is a maintainer trap.

Failure mode: a caller passes a chain of length 3 and forgets to provide all three kinds (passes empty kinds slice, or kinds[0]=Leaf alone). Every cert after kinds.len() is classified as IntermediateCa. Leaf-only lints silently return NotApplicable on what is actually a leaf cert. The compliance report looks clean — until an auditor notices the leaf lints never fire.

Better default: panic-or-error on len mismatch. A truncated kinds slice is almost certainly a caller bug, never a deliberate API use. If the convenience of partial kinds is wanted, expose a separate run_chain_with_inferred_kinds(chain) that walks BasicConstraints to decide.

Maintainer consequence: this is the exact 'silently passing' failure that produces 'pkix-lint missed this' tickets that take an afternoon to root-cause. The current API makes the right thing harder than the wrong thing.

Counterargument: the alternative (panicking on len mismatch) breaks ergonomics for callers who pass a single-element chain and want auto-classification. Fix the panic case by introducing a SubjectKindList enum: { Explicit(Vec), AllLeaf, AllIntermediate, Inferred } — caller picks intent. Or simpler: take Option<&[SubjectKind]> and panic when Some(s) where s.len() != chain.len().
title: LintRunner::run_chain default kind=IntermediateCa silently mis-classifies short kinds slice
